title: Unfaithful Test Doubles (Fantasy Land Tests)
pattern: An hand-written mock, stub, or fake that implements a subset of behavior but is not kept in lockstep with the real production implementation it stands in for.
why_bad: It decouples the test from reality [533]. If the real implementation's behavior changes, the mock remains stale, creating false positives where tests pass successfully while the production application is broken [107, 214].
detection: The presence of manual stubs/fakes in unit tests that lack corresponding role or contract tests executed against the production implementation [118].
counterexample: Using mock configurations that are dynamically verified against schemas or accompanied by shared contract tests [218].
fix: Develop contract tests (such as shared test modules) that run identically against both the test double and the real production implementation to guarantee behavioral alignment [118, 121, 218].
source:
*   *Practical Object-Oriented Design*, "Using Role Tests to Validate Doubles" (p. 227-233) [107, 118, 121]
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Unfaithful doubles" (p. 283) [213, 214, 533]
